1.point: The chapter will show there is no path to God outside the law: the rules we keep and the remembering we lose are one religion at different depths.
steps: The Munajat asks for remembering God and keeping His commands in one breath, as one life.
In our own prayer the two come apart: the form is valid while the remembering is lost.
That gap tempts the conclusion that the law is an outer layer to be shed as one goes deeper, and some traditions taught this.
The masters of the Islamic path taught the opposite, and this chapter sets out why.

2.point: Path and truth are the inward depths of the law's own acts, so each is reached only through the one before it and none can be skipped.
steps: Define the law as the outward acts the Prophet taught.
Define the path as the way from the law to nearness and the truth as what is seen at the end of the path.
Show the path is not a second set of acts: two outwardly identical prayers can differ only inwardly, and that inward way is the path.
So the three are one reality at three depths (shell, core, kernel), all present in a single prayer.
The order runs one way: law without path is possible, path without law is not.
Therefore each depth is reached only through the one before (ship, sea, pearl); ʿirfan begins with the shariʿa.

3.point: No wonder, feat or inner experience can substitute for keeping the law.
steps: Someone who claims the truth while dropping the law has left the ship; by Kubra's test they are liars.
The lie is in the claim, not the feat: such wonders are magic, not karama.
Why the law cannot be bypassed: law builds character, character opens knowledge of God, and each link needs the one before.
What arrives without the law is counterfeit and easily mistaken for the real light.
Even genuine experiences on the true path are preliminary; what counts is lasting change.
That lasting change is produced by lifelong keeping of the law, not by a forty-day exercise.

4.point: The inner work does not begin somewhere beyond the law; it begins inside the prayer, with attention at Allahu akbar.
steps: The path deepens the acts of the law we already perform, starting with knowing what we say at Allahu akbar.
Knowing what we say needs attention, and attention cannot be held by force.
The difficulty is a circle: heartfelt words need a knowledge that only comes from attentive practice.
The faculty of attention is not missing (a book can absorb us); the habit of bringing it to prayer is.
That habit is built a degree at a time, inside the law.

5.point: The law is kept to the last breath; at the end of the road only the reason for keeping it changes, from growth to thanks.
steps: The claim that advanced travellers are released from the law is rejected outright.
Proof: the Prophet, who went furthest, kept every precept to his last moments, so no station releases anyone.
If anything, the unveiled truth makes observance stricter; release is a confusion about the stages of worship.
Worship has stages: for a growing soul it is the means of growth; for a perfected soul it is no longer for growth.
The Prophet names the remaining reason: thanks; this is what the Munajat at the chapter head asks for.

¶4.why: States the chapter's thesis in the title's terms and previews the structure; the recall of earlier ground is kept to a sentence.

¶5.label: advance

¶6.why: Defines path and truth and their sequence; needed before the inside/outside argument.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Completes the thought experiment: the inward difference is the path, the outward frame is the law, what is seen is the truth. The Khomeini valid/accepted line is used to make the step, not merely added.

¶9.why: The attributed saying maps words/actions/states onto law/path/truth, a mapping ¶8 has already made; nothing later depends on this formulation. A second authority for a step already taken.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Draws the conclusion that the three are one reality at different depths and introduces shell/core/kernel, which the section title and later chapters use. The Hamadani biography clause is dead weight within an otherwise needed paragraph.

¶11.label: support
¶11.why: Gives the example (one salah as service, nearness, arrival) that ¶12 then uses: 'it served, yet it did not draw near'.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Supplies the one-way order: law without path is possible, path without law is not, because the path has nothing else to work on.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Draws the section's conclusion (none can be skipped) and supplies the ship/sea/pearl image that ¶14 argues from.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Applies Kubra's image to the claimant who drops the law: liars, whatever wonders they show.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Explains what 'liars' means, which the point needs: the claim is false and the wonder is magic, not karama.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Supplies the reason the law cannot be bypassed: the chain law, character, knowledge of God.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Adds that each link needs the one before and applies it to the claimants; without this ¶16 would be a list, not an argument.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: New step: what arrives without the law is counterfeit and is mistaken for knowledge of God.

¶20.label: advance

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Closes the section: the lasting change is made by lifelong keeping of the law, contrasted with a forty-day exercise.

¶22.label: advance

¶23.label: advance

¶24.why: The cliff image illustrates a claim ¶23 has already made, that attention cannot be summoned by deciding to; ¶25 moves on to the circle without using the cliff or the 'reason says' framing.

¶35.why: The four journeys and the return among people are not needed for 'the law holds to the last breath; only the reason changes'. Nothing in the section uses it; it is a forward reference to Chapter Sixteen.

¶36.why: Summarises all four sections' conclusions; every claim has already been stated where it was argued.

¶37.label: aside
